assurance: Partial implementation verification: Aeneas-extracted production u64 arithmetic, basket/account operations, model/rate construction and discovery, complete transaction assessment/application and vector candidate filtering refine Lean specifications. This includes validation, original-snapshot evaluation, aggregation, availability/preservation, preparation, runtime conservation diagnostics, atomic multi-account commit and receipts. Explicit collection/Arc/UTF-8 models, lawful identifier operations, resource bounds, compiler/translation and primitive models remain trusted. Execution/replay, observations, remaining public data APIs and other numeric backends remain open.

limitations: The generic Nat specifications are proved. The separate u64_checked_arithmetic contract refines the extracted u64 implementation; arbitrary QuantityScalar laws are not proved.
BigUint/BigInt, serialization, and user-defined trait laws remain legacy refinement gaps. Signed u64 weighting is covered by the separate runtime_linear_conservation implementation contract.

Proves total correctness of the Aeneas-generated production call paths for all u64 operand pairs in the default-feature configuration. Rust MIR inlining, Charon/Aeneas translation, and compiler/codegen correctness are trusted rather than proved here.

Primitive semantics come from Aeneas and explicit adapters for u64 add_with_overflow, mul_with_overflow, and the cold_path hint. The checker rejects other intrinsic instantiations and changes to the external template. See verification/AENEAS.md.
Does not cover BigUint, arbitrary QuantityScalar backends, signed weighted conversion, serialization, accounts, or exchanges. Rust retains its generic trait bounds and strong types.

Proves termination and exact constructor results for all finite Vec inputs represented by Aeneas, all u64 quantities, and arbitrary typed assets with total equality agreeing with identity. First duplicate rejection includes zero quantities; successful output preserves nonzero values and order.

The shared-source harness compiles the exact production files before drop elaboration. Public forwarding and the thin retain adapter are checked syntactically. Rust MIR, Charon/Aeneas translation, compiler/codegen, primitive and Vec iterator semantics remain trusted. See verification/BASKETS.md.

IndexMap lookup, insertion, and ordered retention use explicit executable models. Their implementation, lawful/stable Eq and Hash, successful allocation, resizing, and destructor effects are outside the proof. Hash internals fail closed in the model and are never called by the logical map.

The theorem specializes the shared constructor to u64 vector inputs. Arbitrary iterators, BigUint/custom numeric backends, asset-qualified conversion, and serialization implementations are not refined. The public API retains its original strong types and trait bounds; adapters have finite conformance tests.
Does not establish basket mutation/shortfall refinement or account/exchange correctness. Those remain separate contracts.

Production checked_add, checked_scale, contains and PartialEq::eq are shared-source extracted for u64. Theorems prove total execution and exact ordered natural-number updates/errors, containment and order-independent equality. Equality is equivalent to permutation for unique keys and requires lengths representable by usize. Containment requires unique requested keys. Asset equality/cloning must satisfy the existing explicit laws.

Canonical representation proofs establish unique keys and no zero entries through store, credit/debit, addition, scaling, shortfall and successful account staging. They compose with the extracted operations; they do not prove physical memory layout or allocation bounds.

The ordered-map model and compiler/MIR/Charon/Aeneas/primitive trust remain. Option equality and bounded map length have explicit executable adapters; no new axioms are added. Out-of-range logical map lengths fail closed. Physical hashing/allocation/destructor/clone isolation are outside the proof. See verification/BASKETS.md.

Only local loop bindings were renamed for extraction, and equality uses a short-circuiting loop instead of unsupported Iterator::all while preserving PartialEq::eq dispatch and existing public bounds. Arbitrary iterators, sorted views, serialization, numeric backend laws and full exchange behavior remain separate contracts.
Asset domains remain separate Lean and Rust type parameters. The round-trip theorem is about the Lean structure; Rust conversions are covered by tests and compiler checks.

Entry canonicalization and shortfall have design proofs. Separate basket/account implementation contracts now cover construction, lookup, insertion/removal, shortfall, addition/scaling, containment/equality and logical canonical representation preservation. Sorted iteration, remaining typed adapters, physical IndexMap semantics and serialization remain unrefined.

The actual production deposit, withdrawal, shortfall, basket lookup/insertion, and checked arithmetic call paths are extracted from shared source. For u64 quantities and finite baskets, Lean proves execution without panic/divergence and exact natural-number outcomes, including ordered state and errors. Withdrawal and shortfall require distinct requested asset identifiers, as enforced by the public Basket representation.

Generic assets require total equality agreeing with identity and total identity-preserving Clone. Rust Eq/Clone/Hash trait bounds alone do not establish those laws. Concrete equality and clone dictionaries witness satisfiability; the premises do not assume update correctness.

IndexMap storage, iteration, lookup, insertion, removal, cloning, allocation, and hashing use the explicit ordered-list model. Models invoke supplied equality and asset/value cloning, but physical allocator/hash/hasher-clone/destructor behavior remains trusted. Compiler, MIR, Charon/Aeneas translation and backend primitives are also trusted. See verification/ACCOUNTS.md.

QuantityMeasure groups exactly the pre-existing SignedMeasure trait bounds and has a blanket implementation; all public Rust scalar requirements remain. The generated account proof retains the QuantityScalar dictionary. Unused formatting and hashing paths fail closed in the model. Exact signed conversion is now covered by the separate runtime_linear_conservation contract.

Does not refine arbitrary QuantityScalar backends, BigUint/BigInt, serialization, account cloning as a separate API, account identifiers in Economy, full exchange preparation/commit (per-account staging has a separate refinement contract), or replay. These remain separate contracts.

The pinned Lean backend has a checksum-guarded patch that gives generated discriminant instances fully qualified names. It fixes cross-module name collisions without changing enum values, program translation, or proof semantics; the kernel checks the resulting declarations.

The production crate-private Account::prepare_exchange helper is shared-source extracted for u64 quantities. Lean proves termination and exact ordered natural-number results/errors of cloning, withdrawal then deposit, including shortfall rejection and overflow after successful withdrawal. Unique consumed assets and lawful equality/cloning are required; successful preparation is not assumed.

The helper borrows its source immutably in Rust and returns a new account only on success. preparedOutcome models publication or original-state retention for conformance; its atomicity theorem does not prove the multi-account commit loop. Existing collection/clone isolation, allocation, stable hashing, compiler/MIR, Charon/Aeneas and primitive-model assumptions remain; no new external model is introduced. See verification/ACCOUNTS.md.

The production prepare_effects caller delegates the clone-withdraw-deposit sequence to this helper. Its handoff is syntactically guarded. The separate complete_transactions contract now extracts and proves the caller through full analyze/assess/apply; 492 earlier staging fixtures and 596 complete transaction fixtures supplement those proofs.

The generic Rust API and ownership/type guarantees are preserved. The theorem does not establish arbitrary QuantityScalar laws, BigUint/BigInt correctness, physical collection correctness, serialization or replay.

These original design theorems assume a typed lookup context. The separate snapshot_evaluation implementation contract covers recursive expression/condition evaluation, actual lookup and exact typed errors; complete_transactions now composes the full validation, condition and effect orchestration in Economy::analyze.

Effect merge algebra is over exact Nat; no claim is made that diagnostic order or bounded overflow is independent of insertion order. The separate bounded_effect_helpers contract covers production checked scaling-plus-addition and single-quantity merging, including atomic failure; it does not cover the complete per-account aggregation loop.

These original design theorems begin with distinct already-aggregated account/asset effects. The separate complete_transactions implementation contract now derives aggregation/caller invariants and covers the full u64 preflight, preparation, error ordering, commit, receipt and internal expect paths.
The scalar static fixture adapter exercises u64 scaling and requirement overflow but is not a proof of the complete Rust rate evaluator.

Arbitrary signed mathematical weights are proved algebraically. The separate runtime_linear_conservation implementation contract covers checked i128 delta accumulation, intermediate overflow and conservation. complete_transactions composes that runtime predicate and whole-state measurements with exact caller diagnostics and transaction behavior.

The production u64 fork, simulate, replay, replayed and Trace new/default/push/exchanges/into_exchanges paths are shared-source extracted. Derived Economy and Exchange clones are proved exact under lawful identifier cloning. Replay terminates without panic for every bounded trace satisfying the transaction metadata/name/capacity preconditions; no successful step or intermediate-state readiness is assumed. The transaction frame derives unchanged rules, invariants and account-key cardinality through every step.

The typed ordered replay specification retains the final state on both success and failure. Rejection atomicity derives exactly the accepted prefix state and first error; success retains receipt order and each receipt describes its own intermediate committed state. Simulation and replayed publish isolated branch results with the source immutably borrowed. The reusable invariant-composition lemma requires a step law; concrete replay refinement discharges the transaction caller invariants through the extracted apply frame, rather than assuming them for intermediate states. The actual analyze/apply accepted control flow also establishes every registered weighted-transfer conservation check; replay_conserves derives exact mathematical consumed/produced equality per receipt throughout a successful trace, and the first-error theorem supplies its successful prefix.

Logical IndexMap, ordered BTreeMap, Vec/slice and Arc models, lawful equality/ordering/hash coherence, UTF-8 lengths, allocation/resources, compiler/MIR/Charon/Aeneas/backend semantics remain explicit trust boundaries. BTreeMap clone calls every key/value clone and preserves entry order; physical tree/Arc storage, reference counts, allocator behavior and clone/COW isolation are not verified. Strong Rust domains and ownership remain enforced. This is not machine-code verification.

Trace generic extend, remaining derived/convenience APIs, serialization/schema contracts and BigUint/BigInt/custom numeric laws remain separate items 16–18. 246 Lean-generated replay scenarios and 596 transaction simulation scenarios supplement the general proofs; they do not replace them.

The model treats account presence as a domain precondition and proves extensional projections. Missing-account distinctions, sorted observation keys, state fingerprints and Rust view refinement are not proved.

Lean keeps semantic domains typed; Rust compile-fail examples independently enforce asset/role identity and immutable inspection. This is not a theorem about rustc, dependency code, package resolution or generic backend laws.
Core dependency and lockfile edits invalidate this review, including transitive updates; their implementation correctness is outside the initial proof boundary.

Shared-source extraction covers try_consume, try_produce and try_preserve for u64 quantities. Theorems prove total execution, exact ordered basket merge/error results, role registration including empty baskets, and unchanged other effect maps, distinctness declarations, computed effects and conditions. Private merge entry/backward-function behavior is proved explicitly.

Roles and assets remain separate generic types. Asset equality and asset/role cloning must satisfy the existing identity/totality laws. Role comparison must terminate and agree with the pure comparator; registered-role identity additionally requires comparison equality to imply identity. Concrete u64 ordering witnesses show these premises are satisfiable. Existing arithmetic refinement relates bounded u64 additions to natural numbers.

BTreeMap/BTreeSet use a new explicit sorted-list model with occupied/vacant entry positions, stored-key retention and default insertion. Applying the model assumes valid ordered collections, lawful total ordering, allocator/tree correctness, clone isolation and the compiler/MIR/Charon/Aeneas/backend boundary. Physical tree code is not verified. See verification/ACCOUNTS.md.

The infallible static convenience-constructor panic contracts and serialization remain separate contracts. Model/rate constructors and computed role/parameter/asset discovery are covered by the model_construction, computed_rate_construction and rate_discovery contracts.

The production LinearInvariant::conserves path and both nested loops are extracted for u64/i128. For all u64 quantities and i64 weights, Lean proves exact widening/weighting, checked intermediate addition, total execution and exact Option Bool agreement with an ordered mathematical Int specification. Some(true) implies equal mathematical weighted consumed/produced totals. None represents intermediate overflow, including cancellation-sensitive order. Whole-state LinearInvariant::measure also refines the ordered checked integer fold across all accounts and assets, including empty accounts, missing weights and intermediate overflow.

Asset equality is total and agrees with identity. Account IDs and assets remain separate types; preserved quantities are retained in the typed delta but not counted as transfers. Missing weights contribute zero. IndexMap and slice iteration use the documented logical collection/backend models; compiler/MIR, Charon/Aeneas, primitive conversion semantics, allocation and physical storage remain trusted. No new axioms or success premises are introduced. Read-only Arc access returns the logical account value; IndexMap values iteration preserves insertion order. Reference counts, mutation/COW and allocator correctness are not proved.

The u64-to-i128 adapter now implements exact widening instead of failing closed, and Option try adapters propagate Some/None. Formatting and hash internals still fail closed. The proof does not claim physical collection correctness.

Invariant constructors remain a separate public-boundary obligation. complete_transactions now proves economy caller classification, diagnostic totals and composition with aggregation/staging/commit. BigUint/BigInt and custom QuantityScalar/QuantityMeasure laws remain open. Whole-state measurement preserves ordered checked arithmetic.

The shared-source recursive production evaluator is proved for all finite expressions and u64 inputs against checked Nat arithmetic. It reads one immutable proposal/account context, evaluates left before right, distinguishes missing parameters/unbound roles/missing accounts, treats absent asset balances as zero, and refines all six binary operations. Both condition operands use that context; all three comparisons and exact error precedence are proved. No successful-execution premise is assumed.

AccountId, Role, Asset and RateId remain distinct generic types. Equality on account IDs/assets and ordering on roles obey the existing total/lawful dictionaries. Sorted BTreeMap lookup and IndexMap lookup preserve logical entries; read-only Arc deref/AsRef exposes its logical pointee. Physical storage, total ordering/hash coherence, allocation, UTF-8 string comparison/cloning, compiler/MIR, Charon/Aeneas and backend semantics remain trusted.

Private evaluator failures are now a typed ExpressionError; the public string API is unchanged. Exact message rendering is proved, including arbitrary valid Unicode parameter names, provided the full message byte length fits usize. Explicit UTF-8 decode/encode and checked push_str models reject malformed slices or oversized strings. Allocation, stack/resource exhaustion, reference counts, COW and machine code are outside the theorem. Formatting internals still fail closed; the proof does not model erased format arguments as arbitrary correct text.

A production condition helper factors the existing evaluations/comparison with unchanged typed signatures and diagnostic order. complete_transactions now composes the full condition iteration, wrapping, aggregation and commit. Serialization and custom numeric backends remain separate obligations.

Production merge_scaled scales source assets with checked multiplication in source order, then atomically adds the resulting basket. Scaling or addition errors return the exact first overflowing asset and the original target. Production merge_quantity performs one checked addition and canonical insertion; computed quantities are not multiplied by units. Theorems relate results and ordered state directly to Nat specifications for all u64 values.

The existing lawful asset equality/cloning and collection/primitive models apply. Immutable source borrows and distinct Rust domains remain intact. complete_transactions now derives and proves role-to-account aggregation, computed evaluation order, availability/preservation, unique affected accounts and complete preparation/commit.

Extracted EconomyBuilder new/default/account/rate/invariant/build for u64, with separate account, asset, role and rate types. Exact ordered duplicate issues, first-entry retention, unaffected fields and complete accepted contents. Build requires distinct account/rate keys; the constructor and insertion/invariant preservation theorems establish this reachable-state invariant.

Appending an issue or invariant requires its current Vec length below usize::MAX; the stronger insertion contract imposes the issue bound even for a fresh ID. Logical map insertion/owning iteration and Arc::new are trusted executable dependency models; physical storage, hashing, allocation, reference counts, COW, clone isolation, destructors and the compiler/MIR/translation/backend boundary remain outside the proof.

Registration preserves the supplied typed account, rate and invariant values; their separate constructors/contracts are not inferred from this theorem. Model serialization and arbitrary numeric backends remain separate contracts.

Extracted u64 Rate new/default, all three computed-effect constructors, condition construction for String labels, distinct-pair canonicalization and recursive referenced-role registration. Exact effect/condition append order, duplicate role/pair handling and unchanged other fields. Arbitrary Into<String> callbacks are not covered by the String forwarding specialization.

Role cloning/ordering must terminate and agree with their logical values/comparator; membership additionally needs comparator equality to imply identity. Distinct construction requires the selected PartialOrd::le to agree with the same comparator; u64 witnesses discharge these laws. Valid ordered collections and lawful total ordering remain assumptions when applying the sorted-list external model to Rust.

Vec append requires a spare usize element. Borrowed-reference ordering and tuple lexicographic cmp/partial_cmp/eq have explicit logical models. Unused tuple lt/le/ge remain fail-closed because pinned Rust chaining hooks are absent from the backend dictionary. Physical trees/storage, allocation/stack limits, cloning, compiler/MIR/translation/backend semantics remain trusted. Static convenience panics, LinearInvariant constructors, serialization and non-u64 numeric backends remain separate contracts.

All ten recursive expression constructors and complete Rate parameter_names/computed_asset_keys paths are extracted. Parameters are the sorted logical union of every computed expression and both sides of every condition. Asset output preserves every occurrence and exact consume/produce/preserve/condition order, with each computed target asset before expression references. Public outputs remain borrowed &str/&Asset in Rust.

Each parameter UTF-8 byte length must fit usize, and the full asset-reference vector length must fit usize. Exact UTF-8 decoding and string ordering, Vec/slice iteration and sorted sets are explicit dependency models. Allocation, recursion/stack limits, physical string/collection storage and the compiler/MIR/translation/backend boundary remain trusted; malformed modeled UTF-8 fails closed.

Metadata discovery composes with structural_validation and complete_transactions. Builder proofs establish computed-target registration; arbitrary deserialization representation contracts remain open. Static basket assets intentionally remain excluded from computed_asset_keys.

Complete extracted u64 structural helper and all seven loops terminate and return the exact stored rate or ordered issues under the logical collection model. Covers zero units, missing-rate early return, missing/unknown roles and parameters, distinct-role violations and sorted deduplicated missing accounts. Actual acceptance yields nonzero units, required bindings to existing accounts, required parameters and distinctness; actual rejection is nonempty.

Account/rate/role identity cloning and selected equality/ordering operations must obey explicit laws. Account comparator equality must imply identity for the existence corollary. Valid sorted BTreeMap/BTreeSet representations, lawful ordering/equality/hash coherence, borrowed UTF-8 representation, allocation, physical collection/Arc/string semantics, compiler/MIR/Charon/Aeneas/backend correctness remain trusted.

Parameter names must fit usize in UTF-8, and a conservative maximum issue count must fit usize. These are resource premises, not assumed validation success. Required-name iteration clones a set of borrowed names to avoid unsupported nested shared borrows; this adds a temporary allocation while preserving public types and diagnostic order.

Economy::analyze calls the borrowed-result helper through a guarded handoff. complete_transactions now proves the caller orchestration, derived lookup/expect safety, aggregation, availability, preparation, commit and receipts. Arbitrary deserialized metadata and other numeric backends remain separate obligations.

The complete production u64 analyze, assess and apply paths are freshly extracted. Refinement proves termination without panic and exact natural-number/signed-integer results, ordered diagnostics and state, including structural rejection, original-snapshot conditions/computed expressions, static scaling, unscaled preservation and computed quantities, alias aggregation, complete shortfalls, preparation and invariant diagnostics. The contracts do not assume successful validation, feasibility, conservation or a successful commit.

Apply returns the exact specified proposal and deltas. Successful preparation relates every staged account to its original balance and aggregated effects, with unique existing account IDs. Apply discharges both expect preconditions and every mutable index lookup, preserves the entire raw model on rejection, and preserves account order/keys, rates, invariants and accounts outside the receipt deltas on success. Typed semantic domains remain separate Rust/Lean parameters. The accepted_receipt_refines corollary explicitly proves unique receipt accounts and, for each delta, that the committed observable account equals successful consumption-then-production of its original balance.

Model identifier/asset/role equality and cloning must be lawful and terminating; comparison must agree with the logical comparator. Account ordering additionally requires reflexivity, identity-consistent equality, strict-order transitivity and reversal. Computed targets must be registered; the included actual new/static/computed/condition/distinct builder proofs establish and preserve that representation invariant. UTF-8 diagnostic/parameter/discovery lengths, validation issue growth and account count have explicit usize bounds. These are input/representation/resource laws, not assumptions of transaction correctness.

Canonical aggregation, sorted unique affected accounts, existing-account lookup and effect-count bounds are derived from validation and builder invariants; they discharge preflight, preparation and commit obligations. The sorted logical BTreeMap/BTreeSet and ordered IndexMap abstractions, allocator, stable hashing, identity-preserving clones, Rust compiler/MIR, Charon/Aeneas and primitive models remain trusted. New mutable-index adapters panic on absent keys and preserve all other entries; Arc clone exposes the same immutable logical pointee without verifying physical reference counting or copy-on-write.

Filtering refines the public implementation for finite Vec candidates: exact stable filtering including duplicates against one original snapshot, with a successful boolean assessment for every candidate. Arbitrary user-provided iterator behavior, resource allocation, destructor effects, generic numeric laws, BigUint/BigInt, serialization/schema, formatting, other convenience APIs, fork/simulation, replay, observations and canonical keys remain separate contracts. No fingerprint collision-freedom claim is made.

The 596 Lean-generated full-transaction cases check exact assessments, errors, receipts, final account order/state, rejection atomicity, unchanged rates/invariants, and filtering through the public Rust API. Conformance is finite evidence supplementing the general refinement proofs. Mutation controls regenerate compilable production Rust changes and require the semantic proofs to reject them. See verification/ACCOUNTS.md for source refactors and the precise trust boundary.
